responsibility: Implements rustc’s GCC-based code generation backend, turning Rust monomorphized MIR and type/layout information into libgccjit IR, emitting final compilation artifacts, and integrating that backend with rustc’s codegen interfaces. The crate entry point in `lib.rs` defines the backend surface, owns top-level synchronized GCC state and target information, implements `CodegenBackend`/`WriteBackendMethods`, and delegates to the rest of the crate. Per-codegen-unit compilation is orchestrated by `base.rs`, which configures gccjit contexts from session options, orders and defines monomorphized items, finalizes debuginfo, and produces `ModuleCodegen`s, while `back` provides the backend-emission layer that writes assembly, object files, bitcode/IR placeholders, GCC-specific embedded-LTO combinations, and packaged `CompiledModule` results. `archive.rs` connects generated objects to rustc’s archive packaging path for static libraries. The central lowering state lives in `context.rs`, which owns the libgccjit context, caches, symbol maps, ABI/layout metadata, and shared backend state used across code generation. MIR and backend IR construction is primarily implemented by `builder.rs`, which supplies the main SSA/codegen operations; `int.rs` extends this with integer-semantics support and helper-call lowering for targets or libgccjit configurations that cannot directly model all Rust integer operations, especially wide integers; `asm.rs` lowers Rust inline and global assembly into GCC extended asm forms; and `coverageinfo.rs` provides the backend hook point for MIR coverage instrumentation emission. Call and data ABI lowering is handled by `abi.rs`, which maps Rust `FnAbi` and argument-passing conventions into libgccjit function signatures and stack-parameter handling, while `callee.rs` resolves rustc `Instance`s into callable declarations with the proper ABI, visibility, and attributes, and `declare.rs` creates and registers functions, globals, entry points, and intrinsics in the backend symbol tables. Monomorphized item setup is split so `mono_item.rs` predefines functions and statics with stable linkage/visibility before bodies are emitted, and `consts.rs` lowers statics and constant allocations into GCC globals and initializers with correct alignment, TLS, linkage, visibility, and relocation handling. Type and constant construction utilities are provided by `common.rs`, which offers shared helpers for constants, strings, vectors, null/undef values, pointer checks, and type-sign reflection; `type_.rs`, which constructs and classifies GCC primitive, aggregate, pointer, vector, and function types; and `type_of.rs`, which translates rustc layouts and `TyAndLayout` information into cached concrete gccjit types. Backend support for Rust runtime conventions includes `allocator.rs`, which emits allocator shim entry points, allocation-error handlers, and exported globals describing allocator/OOM behavior. Intrinsic lowering is centralized in `intrinsic`, which dispatches Rust intrinsics, maps libc and custom shims, translates LLVM intrinsic names to GCC builtins with target-specific fallback tables, and lowers generic SIMD intrinsics into gccjit vector operations. Source-level debugging integration is provided by `debuginfo.rs`, which maps spans and scopes to GCC locations and debug contexts and tracks builder debug locations. Finally, `errors.rs` defines the backend-specific diagnostics used to report GCC backend limitations and configuration problems. Together, these modules make `rustc_codegen_gcc` the compiler component responsible for translating Rust code into GCC-backed machine-code artifacts and related metadata through the rustc codegen pipeline.
